question_text: Form a quadratic equation whose roots are 7 ± 2√5.

recall_prompt: Say how you would form the equation — say what two numbers you compute from the roots and which formula you put them into.
insider_note: The whole first mark is one square: (2√5)² = 4·5 = 20, not 10. The surds already cancel in the sum on their own — the product is where this question is decided.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Sum and product
steps.margin_note: First mark. The surd parts cancel in the sum: 7 + 2√5 + 7 − 2√5 = 14. The product is (7)² − (2√5)² = 49 − 4·5 = 29; remember (2√5)² = 4 × 5, not 2 × 5.

recall.must_convey: That the two roots are added to get 14 and multiplied, as a difference of two squares, to get 49 − 20 = 29.
accept: add the roots to get fourteen and multiply them to get forty nine minus twenty which is twenty nine
sum is fourteen, product is seven squared minus two root five squared equals twenty nine
the surds cancel in the sum and the product is a difference of two squares
roots add cheste fourteen, multiply cheste forty nine minus twenty is twenty nine

steps.why: A quadratic is fixed by the sum and product of its roots, so those two numbers are all the question really asks for. Conjugate surds are chosen so that both come out rational.
common_mistakes: Getting the product as 49 + 20 = 69 by mis-applying (a + b)(a − b).
Trying to expand (x − 7 − 2√5)(x − 7 + 2√5) directly and making a surd error.

steps.label: Write the equation
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The formula has a MINUS before the sum and a PLUS before the product. Write '= 0' — an expression is not an equation.

recall.must_convey: That the equation is x² − (sum)x + (product) = 0, giving x² − 14x + 29 = 0.
accept: x squared minus sum x plus product equals zero gives x squared minus fourteen x plus twenty nine

steps.why: x² − (α + β)x + αβ = (x − α)(x − β), so this formula gives exactly the quadratic with those two roots and leading coefficient 1.
common_mistakes: Writing x² + 14x + 29 = 0 with the wrong sign on the sum.
